label: Wave
short: A pattern that repeats in space and time and carries energy without carrying matter along, like ripples on water.

label: Frequency
short: How many times per second a wave repeats. Written with the Greek letter nu or f.

label: Amplitude
short: How tall a wave is, measured from its resting level to its peak.

label: Wave-particle duality
short: The finding that things like electrons and light sometimes behave like tiny lumps and sometimes like spreading waves, depending on how you look.

label: Photon
short: A single packet of light. Its energy is the Planck constant times the light's frequency.

label: Planck constant
short: A fixed number, written h, that links the energy of a light packet to its frequency. Its value is fixed exactly by the definition of the SI units.

label: de Broglie wavelength
short: The wavelength that goes with a moving particle: the Planck constant divided by the particle's momentum.

label: Quantization
short: The fact that some quantities, such as the energy of an electron held in a small region, can only take certain separate values, not any value in between.

label: Boundary condition
short: A rule about what a wave must do at the edge of the region it lives in, for example that it must be zero at a wall.

label: Node
short: A place where a wave is exactly zero. For a wave trapped in a box, more nodes means more energy.

label: Quantum state
short: A complete description of what is known about a quantum system, from which the chances of every measurement result can be worked out.

label: Wavefunction
short: A function, written with the Greek letter psi, that describes the quantum state of a particle. Its squared size tells you how likely you are to find the particle at each place.

label: Probability density
short: How concentrated the chance of finding a particle is at each point. Adding it up over a region gives the chance of finding the particle there.

label: Superposition
short: A state made by adding two or more states together. A particle in a superposition has no single definite value for the property in which the states differ.

label: Uncertainty principle
short: The rule that a particle's position and momentum cannot both be known exactly at once; squeezing one makes the other spread out.

label: Energy level
short: One of the separate energy values that a bound electron is allowed to have.

label: Ground state
short: The lowest-energy state of a system.

label: Excited state
short: Any state of a system with more energy than its ground state.

label: Degenerate
short: Describes different states that happen to have exactly the same energy.

label: Schrodinger equation
short: The equation that says how a quantum state behaves. Solving it for an electron in a given surrounding gives the allowed energies and wavefunctions.

label: Hamiltonian
short: The recipe for the total energy of a system, written as an operator. The Schrodinger equation uses it to find the allowed states.

label: Orbital
short: A wavefunction for a single electron. The shape of its squared size is the familiar cloud picture of where that electron is likely to be.

label: Quantum number
short: A whole number (or half-whole number) that labels a state, for example n, l and m for an electron in an atom.

label: s, p, d and f orbitals
short: Letters used for orbital shapes: s is a sphere, p has two lobes, d and f have more complicated lobes. They correspond to the values 0, 1, 2 and 3 of the angular quantum number l.

label: Spin
short: A built-in property of electrons that behaves like a tiny magnet with only two possible orientations, usually called up and down.

label: Fermion
short: A kind of particle, such as the electron, that obeys the Pauli exclusion principle.

label: Pauli exclusion principle
short: The rule that two electrons cannot be in exactly the same state, which is why atoms fill up shell by shell.

label: Coulomb interaction
short: The push or pull between electric charges: like charges repel and opposite charges attract.

label: Many-body problem
short: The difficulty that the motion of every electron depends on every other electron, so the equations cannot be solved exactly for more than a few particles.

label: Born-Oppenheimer approximation
short: The simplification of treating the nuclei as standing still while the much lighter electrons settle around them.

label: Electron density
short: How much electronic charge there is at each point in space. It is a single function of position, unlike the wavefunction of many electrons.

label: Exchange
short: The energy that comes from the Pauli principle: electrons with the same spin cannot share a state, so they keep apart and repel each other less than a plain average would suggest. It has no classical counterpart.

label: Exchange and correlation
short: The parts of the electron-electron interaction that come from the Pauli principle (exchange) and from electrons avoiding each other (correlation). Density functional theory has to approximate them.

label: Functional
short: A rule that takes a whole function as input and returns a single number. The energy as a function of the electron density is a functional.

label: Hohenberg-Kohn theorems
short: Two results showing that the ground-state electron density alone determines the energy and everything else about the system.

label: Kohn-Sham equations
short: A set of one-electron equations whose solution gives the exact ground-state density, if the exchange-correlation part were known exactly.

label: Self-consistent field
short: A loop that guesses the electron density, works out the potential the electrons would feel in that density, solves for a new density, and repeats until the density stops changing.

label: DFT (density functional theory)
short: A way of computing the energy and properties of atoms, molecules and solids from the electron density instead of the full many-electron wavefunction.

label: Periodic boundary conditions
short: A trick for modelling a solid: a small cell is repeated endlessly in all directions so that it behaves as part of an infinite crystal.

label: Unit cell
short: The smallest box that, repeated in every direction, builds the whole crystal.

label: Plane wave
short: A wave of constant size that ripples evenly through space. VASP builds its wavefunctions from many of them.

label: Pseudopotential
short: A smoothed stand-in for the nucleus and its tightly bound inner electrons, so that only the outer electrons need to be computed.

label: Simulation
short: A calculation on a computer that imitates a real system, so you can study it without building it.

label: Atom
short: The basic building block of ordinary matter: a tiny, heavy nucleus surrounded by a cloud of lighter electrons.

label: Electron
short: A very light particle with negative charge. Electrons around the nuclei decide how atoms bond and how a material conducts electricity and absorbs light.

label: Nucleus
short: The tiny, heavy centre of an atom, made of protons and neutrons. In most calculations here the nuclei are treated as fixed points.

label: Quantum mechanics
short: The set of rules that describes how very small things such as electrons behave. It replaces the everyday picture of tiny balls on tracks.

label: Approximation
short: A deliberate simplification that makes a calculation possible at the cost of some accuracy. Every practical method uses some.

label: Basis set
short: A fixed collection of simple building-block functions that are added together to describe a wavefunction or a density. A bigger set describes it better and costs more.

label: Supercell
short: A block of several unit cells joined together and repeated through space, used to model defects, surfaces or bigger arrangements of atoms.

label: Perovskite
short: A crystal family with formula ABX3: small B cations sit inside corner-sharing octahedra of X anions, and large A cations fill the gaps between the octahedra. Many oxides, such as SrTiO3, have this structure.

label: Octahedral tilting
short: A cooperative rotation of the corner-sharing BX6 octahedra of a perovskite, which happens when the A cation is too small for its cavity. It lowers the symmetry and enlarges the repeating cell.

label: Tolerance factor
short: A number made from ionic radii that says how well the A, B and X ions of a perovskite fit together. Goldschmidt's t near 1 suits the ideal cubic structure; lower values point to tilted octahedra. It is a rule of thumb, not a stability calculation.

label: Ionic radius
short: A tabulated size for an ion, chosen so that sums of radii reproduce measured bond lengths. It depends on the charge of the ion, how many neighbours it has and, for some ions, its spin state.

label: Property
short: Anything you can measure or compute about a material, such as its energy, its shape, its band gap or how much it conducts.

label: Scaling
short: How the cost of a calculation grows as the system gets bigger. Cost proportional to size to the power 3 is called cubic scaling.

label: Force field
short: A set of fixed, simple rules for the forces between atoms, without any electrons in the calculation. Very fast, and only as good as the rules.

label: Hartree-Fock
short: A method that treats each electron as moving in the average field of all the others. It leaves out part of how electrons avoid each other.

label: Coupled cluster
short: A family of high-accuracy methods that add electron-electron effects step by step. Accurate for small molecules and expensive for large systems.

label: VASP
short: The Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package, a program that computes the energy and electronic structure of atoms, molecules and solids using DFT with plane waves.

label: Standing wave
short: A wave that does not travel. It stays in place with fixed points of no motion, like a plucked guitar string.

label: Normalization
short: Scaling a wavefunction so that the probabilities over all of space add up to exactly one.

label: Radial node
short: A spherical shell around the nucleus where an orbital's wavefunction is zero, so the electron is never found there.

label: Angular node
short: A flat or cone-shaped surface through the nucleus where an orbital's wavefunction is zero. The number of angular nodes equals l.

label: Electron volt (eV)
short: The energy an electron gains when it moves through one volt. The usual unit of energy for electrons in atoms and solids.

label: Angstrom
short: A unit of length equal to 10^-10 meters. Atoms are a few angstrom apart in a solid.

label: Band
short: A range of closely spaced electron energies that forms when many atoms are brought together in a crystal.

label: Band gap
short: A range of energies between two bands where no electron states exist. Its size helps decide whether a material conducts.

label: Effective mass
short: The mass an electron or hole seems to have when it moves through a crystal, set by how sharply its band curves near an extremum: a strongly curved band means a light carrier.

label: Projected density of states
short: The density of states split into contributions from each atom and orbital (s, p, d, f), found by projecting the states onto spheres around the atoms.

label: Tetrahedron method
short: A way to integrate over the Brillouin zone that splits it into small tetrahedra and interpolates the bands inside each, giving sharp densities of states from a uniform k-point mesh.

label: d-band center
short: The average energy of the d states of an atom, the first moment of its d-projected density of states; on transition-metal surfaces it tracks how strongly adsorbates bind.

label: Charge density difference
short: The density of a combined system minus the densities of its separate parts on the same grid; it shows where bonding moved electrons to and from.

label: Electron localization function (ELF)
short: A number between 0 and 1 at each point in space; values near 1 mark localized electron pairs such as bonds and lone pairs, and 0.5 is the value of a uniform electron gas.

label: Formation energy
short: The energy of a compound minus the energies of its elements in their reference states, usually per atom; a negative value means the compound is lower in energy than the elements.

label: Convex hull
short: The lowest convex envelope of formation energy plotted against composition. A phase on it is stable at 0 K against every mixture of the other phases.

label: Energy above the hull
short: How far, in energy per atom, a phase sits above the convex hull. Zero means stable; a positive value is the energy it would release by splitting into the hull phases below it.

label: Metastable
short: Higher in energy than the most stable arrangement, but held in place by a barrier, so it can still be made and can last.

label: Stress tensor
short: Nine numbers (six independent) that say how the energy of a cell changes when it is stretched or sheared; its average diagonal value gives the pressure.

label: Selective dynamics
short: A POSCAR option that marks each coordinate of each atom as free to move or frozen during a relaxation or molecular dynamics run.

label: Density of states
short: How many electron states are available at each energy, per unit energy.

label: Hilbert space
short: The space of all possible states of a quantum system. Each state is a point, and adding two states gives another state.

label: Slater determinant
short: A way to write a many-electron wavefunction from one-electron orbitals so that swapping two electrons flips the sign, as the Pauli principle requires.

label: Spin orbital
short: An orbital together with a choice of spin up or spin down. Each electron occupies one spin orbital.

label: Correlation
short: The way electrons avoid each other because they repel, beyond what the simplest average-field picture captures.

label: External potential
short: The push or pull on the electrons that comes from outside the electrons themselves, in a solid mainly the attraction of the nuclei.

label: Ground-state density
short: The electron density of the lowest-energy state of a system.

label: Variational principle
short: Any trial state gives an energy at or above the true ground-state energy, so the lowest energy you can find is the best estimate. In DFT the same holds for trial densities.

label: Kohn-Sham orbital
short: A one-electron wavefunction of the imaginary non-interacting system that Kohn and Sham use. Filled with electrons, the orbitals give the same density as the real interacting electrons.

label: Effective potential
short: The single potential that every electron of the Kohn-Sham system feels: the attraction of the nuclei plus the Hartree repulsion plus the exchange-correlation potential. It depends on the density.

label: Hartree potential
short: The classical electrostatic repulsion that an electron feels from the whole electron density, treated as a smooth cloud of charge.

label: Density mixing
short: In each self-consistency step, the new input density is a blend of the old input and the new output, instead of the new output alone. Blending too much can make the loop oscillate; too little makes it slow.

label: Residual (SCF)
short: How far the density that comes out of a self-consistency step is from the density that went in. The loop has converged when the residual is close to zero.

label: Charge sloshing
short: A slow back-and-forth movement of electron charge from one side of a large cell to the other during the self-consistency loop, common in metals, long cells and slabs. Smaller mixing damps it.

label: Cutoff energy
short: The largest kinetic energy of plane wave kept in the basis. In VASP it is ENCUT. Higher means more accurate and slower.

label: k-point
short: One wave vector in reciprocal space at which the orbitals are calculated. A calculation uses a finite set of them to approximate an average over the whole Brillouin zone.

label: Reciprocal lattice
short: The set of wave vectors G for which a plane wave repeats with the crystal lattice. Its spacings are inversely related to the real-space ones.

label: Bloch theorem
short: In a perfect crystal each orbital is a plane wave times a function that repeats with the lattice, so it is labelled by a wave vector k.

label: Brillouin zone
short: The Wigner-Seitz cell of the reciprocal lattice: the region of wave vectors that holds one copy of every distinct Bloch state.

label: Fermi level
short: The energy up to which levels are filled at zero temperature. In a metal it lies inside a band.

label: PAW
short: Projector augmented wave: the plane waves carry a smooth function and a correction inside each atomic sphere restores the true wiggles near the nucleus.

label: Hybrid functional
short: A functional that mixes a fraction of exact (Hartree-Fock) exchange into a semilocal one. More expensive, often better for band gaps.

label: Meta-GGA
short: A functional that also depends on the kinetic-energy density of the orbitals, such as SCAN and r2SCAN.

label: Dispersion correction
short: An added pairwise attraction that stands in for the weak van der Waals force that common functionals miss.

label: Damping function
short: A factor that switches a dispersion correction off at short distances, where the functional already describes the bonding, so the correction acts only between atoms that are far apart.

label: Magnetic moment
short: The difference between the up and down electron counts around an atom or in the cell, in units of the Bohr magneton.

label: Crystal-field splitting
short: The way the five d levels of a metal ion split in energy when the ion is surrounded by neighbours. In an octahedron they split into three lower t2g levels and two higher eg levels.

label: Charge-transfer energy
short: The energy needed to move an electron from a ligand, such as oxygen, onto the metal ion. When it is small or negative, the holes of a highly charged metal ion sit largely on the ligands instead of on the metal.

label: POSCAR
short: The VASP input file that holds the cell, the elements and the position of every atom.

label: INCAR
short: The VASP input file of TAG = value lines that says what to calculate and how carefully.

label: KPOINTS file
short: The VASP input file that says how the Brillouin zone is sampled: a mesh, a path or a list of points.

label: POTCAR
short: The licensed VASP input file with the pseudopotential dataset of each element. This site never shows its contents.

label: OSZICAR
short: A short VASP log with one line per electronic step and one per ionic step, good for watching a run live.

label: OUTCAR
short: The long VASP log of a run: setup, every step, forces, stress, Fermi level and timing.

label: CONTCAR
short: The most recent geometry of a run, written in POSCAR format. It is the structure you restart from.

label: CHGCAR
short: The file with the charge density of the last electronic step, used to restart or to run bands on a fixed density.

label: WAVECAR
short: The large binary file with the wavefunctions. It is the most valuable file to restart from.

label: Restart
short: Starting a new run from the wavefunctions or charge density of an earlier run, chosen with ISTART and ICHARG.

label: Ionic step
short: One move of the atoms (and perhaps the cell) in a relaxation, with a full electronic calculation at each geometry.

label: Job script
short: A short batch file that asks a cluster scheduler for cores and time and then starts VASP.

label: MPI rank
short: One of the parallel processes VASP runs on. NCORE and KPAR decide how the ranks share the work.

label: VASPKIT
short: A free command-line helper that writes VASP inputs and processes outputs through numbered menu codes.

label: Convergence
short: A result has converged when making a setting more demanding no longer changes it by more than you can accept.

label: Pulay stress
short: An artificial pressure that appears when the cell volume changes while the number of plane waves is set for the starting cell. A higher cutoff reduces it.

label: Smearing
short: Spreading the occupation of electron levels over a small energy width (SIGMA) so a sum over k-points settles faster, mainly for metals.

label: NBANDS
short: The number of electron states VASP calculates at each k-point. Too few leaves the top state half filled.

label: Spin polarization
short: Allowing up-spin and down-spin electron densities to differ in a calculation (ISPIN = 2 in VASP).

label: Magnetization density
short: The difference between up-spin and down-spin electron densities at each point in space, m(r) = n_up(r) - n_down(r).

label: Collinear magnetism
short: A magnetic arrangement in which every atomic moment points either parallel or antiparallel to a single axis.

label: Non-collinear magnetism
short: A magnetic arrangement in which atomic moments point along arbitrary 3D directions rather than a single axis.

label: Antiferromagnet
short: A magnetic crystal whose local atomic moments cancel to zero net magnetization over the unit cell.

label: Ferrimagnet
short: A magnetic crystal with opposing sublattice moments of unequal magnitude, leaving a non-zero net moment.

label: Propagation vector
short: A reciprocal-space vector k that describes how magnetic moments repeat or alternate from one cell to the next.

label: Exchange constant
short: The coupling parameter J in a spin Hamiltonian that measures the energy preference for parallel versus antiparallel neighbour spins.

label: Stoner criterion
short: The condition I * N(E_F) > 1 under which spontaneous spin splitting lowers the energy of an itinerant metal.

label: Elastic tensor
short: The 6 by 6 table of elastic constants that links a small strain of the cell to the stress it produces.

label: Voigt notation
short: Writing the pairs xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy as the single indices 1 to 6, so a symmetric strain or stress becomes a list of six numbers.

label: Bulk modulus
short: How hard a material resists a uniform squeeze: the pressure needed per relative change of volume, usually given in GPa.

label: Equation of state
short: A fitted curve of energy (or pressure) against volume, giving the equilibrium volume, the bulk modulus and its pressure derivative.

label: Phonon
short: A quantum of lattice vibration: one normal mode of the atoms moving together at a definite frequency and wave vector.

label: Imaginary mode
short: A vibration whose squared frequency comes out negative, printed as an imaginary frequency; the structure can lower its energy by moving along it.

label: LO-TO splitting
short: In a polar crystal, the long-range dipole field splits the longitudinal and transverse optical modes at the zone centre (Gamma).

label: Dielectric tensor
short: The 3 by 3 tensor that says how strongly a material screens an electric field in each direction, from electrons alone or with the ions too.

label: Born effective charge
short: The change of polarization when one atom is moved, per unit displacement: a 3 by 3 tensor per atom that can differ from the nominal ionic charge.

label: Bader charge
short: The number of electrons inside an atom's region when the density is split along surfaces where it has no slope across them.

label: Kramers-Kronig transform
short: The relation that gives the real part of a response function, such as the dielectric function, from its imaginary part over all frequencies.

label: Scissor shift
short: Rigidly moving the empty bands, or the absorption spectrum, up by a fixed energy to correct an underestimated gap.

label: Magnetocrystalline anisotropy
short: The energy difference between magnetization directions in a crystal, which comes from spin-orbit coupling.

label: Bravais lattice
short: An infinite grid of points in which every point has the same surroundings; there are 14 kinds in three dimensions.

label: Basis (of a crystal)
short: The group of atoms attached to every lattice point; lattice plus basis gives the crystal.

label: Primitive cell
short: The smallest repeating cell of a crystal, holding exactly one lattice point.

label: Conventional cell
short: A larger repeating cell chosen so that its edges follow the symmetry axes, such as the cube of face-centred cubic.

label: Fractional coordinates
short: Atom positions given as fractions of the three lattice vectors; POSCAR calls them Direct.

label: Symmetry operation
short: A rotation, mirror, inversion, screw, glide or translation that maps the crystal onto itself.

label: Point group
short: The set of rotations, mirrors and inversions that leave a crystal looking the same about one point; crystals have 32.

label: Space group
short: The full set of symmetry operations of a crystal, translations included; there are 230 in three dimensions.

label: Wyckoff position
short: A set of sites that the space group maps onto each other, labelled by a multiplicity and a letter such as 4a.

label: Irreducible Brillouin zone
short: The part of the Brillouin zone left after symmetry-equivalent k-points are merged; VASP computes only these points, with weights.

label: Geometry relaxation
short: A calculation that moves the atoms, and optionally the cell, until the forces and stress are small.

label: Potential energy surface
short: The ground-state energy as a function of the positions of all nuclei; relaxations roll downhill on it.

label: FFT grid
short: The real-space grid that VASP uses to switch each wavefunction between plane waves and real space with fast Fourier transforms.

label: Parallel efficiency
short: The speed-up from using p times the resources divided by p; 1 means doubling the cores halves the time.

label: Slab model
short: A few layers of crystal with vacuum above and below, repeated periodically, used to model a surface.

label: Miller indices
short: Three whole numbers (hkl) that name a crystal plane through the inverse of its intercepts with the cell axes.

label: Surface termination
short: Which atomic layer a slab ends on, when a crystal has more than one kind of layer along a direction.

label: Dipole correction
short: A compensating dipole layer placed in the vacuum of an asymmetric slab so that the potential on both sides is flat.

label: Surface energy
short: The energy needed to make a unit area of surface, from slab and bulk energies.

label: Planar average
short: A quantity averaged over planes parallel to the surface, leaving a curve along the normal.

label: Work function
short: The energy needed to take an electron from the Fermi level to the vacuum just outside a surface.

label: Point defect
short: A defect at one site of a crystal: a vacancy, an interstitial, a substitution or an antisite.

label: Vacancy
short: A site of the crystal where an atom is missing.

label: Interstitial
short: An extra atom placed between the regular sites of a crystal.

label: Antisite
short: A defect in which a host atom sits on the site of a different host element, such as Ga on an As site.

label: Defect formation energy
short: The energy to create a defect from the perfect crystal and reservoirs of atoms and electrons.

label: Chemical potential
short: The energy per atom of a reservoir that atoms are taken from or given to, set by the growth conditions.

label: Minimum energy path
short: The lowest-energy route between two minima of the energy surface. At every point on it the force points along the path.

label: Saddle point
short: A point on the energy surface that is a maximum along the reaction path and a minimum in every other direction. It is the transition state.

label: Activation energy
short: The energy of the saddle point minus the energy of the starting minimum: the barrier a process has to cross.

label: Nudged elastic band
short: A method that finds a minimum energy path by relaxing a chain of images joined by springs, keeping only the perpendicular part of the true force and the parallel part of the spring force.

label: Climbing image
short: The highest image of a nudged elastic band, freed from the springs and pushed uphill along the path so that it ends exactly on the saddle point.

label: Molecular dynamics
short: Moving the atoms forward in time step by step with Newton's equations, using forces from a model or from DFT.

label: Thermostat
short: An algorithm that adds or removes kinetic energy during a simulation so that the temperature fluctuates around a target value.

label: Ensemble
short: The set of quantities a simulation holds fixed, such as particle number, volume and energy (NVE) or particle number, volume and temperature (NVT).

label: Mean squared displacement
short: The average of the squared distance the atoms have moved after a time t. Its slope at long times gives the diffusion coefficient.

label: Radial distribution function
short: How the density of neighbours changes with distance from an atom, relative to a uniform gas. Its peaks mark the coordination shells.

label: Machine-learned force field
short: A force field fitted to DFT energies, forces and stresses that predicts them for new structures far faster than DFT, within the range of structures it was trained on.

label: COHP
short: Crystal orbital Hamilton population: the density of states of an atom pair split into bonding and antibonding parts by weighting it with their Hamiltonian matrix element.

label: ICOHP
short: The COHP integrated up to the Fermi level. Its size is a relative measure of how strongly two atoms bond covalently.

label: Charge spilling
short: The fraction of the electron density that a projection onto local orbitals fails to reproduce. LOBSTER prints it as a quality check of the projection.

label: Quasiparticle
short: An added electron or hole together with the response of the electrons around it. Its energy is what photoemission and inverse photoemission measure.

label: GW approximation
short: A many-body method that computes quasiparticle energies from the one-electron Green's function G and the screened Coulomb interaction W.

label: Exciton
short: A bound pair of an excited electron and the hole it left behind. Excitons pull optical absorption below the quasiparticle gap.

label: Bethe-Salpeter equation
short: An equation for electron-hole pairs built on quasiparticle energies, used to compute optical spectra that include excitons.

label: DMFT
short: Dynamical mean-field theory: treats strong local correlation by mapping each correlated site onto an impurity problem that is solved self-consistently.

label: Wannier function
short: A localized orbital made by Fourier transforming the Bloch states of a group of bands. There is one per band and lattice cell.

label: Berry phase
short: A geometric phase that Bloch states pick up around a closed loop in k-space. It gives the electric polarization and the topological invariants of the bands.

label: Topological invariant
short: An integer, such as a Chern number or a Z2 index, that describes a set of bands as a whole and cannot change unless the gap closes.

label: Charge state
short: The net charge q of a defect after it has given electrons to, or taken them from, the Fermi level.

label: Charge transition level
short: The Fermi level at which two charge states of a defect have the same formation energy.
